dimensions.name: structural rhythm
dimensions.justification: the Roosevelt obverse carries no repeated structural element: one head, one legend, one motto, one date, one mint mark. The hair is a mass with strands, and strand DIRECTION is already scored by the phase-2 strand tensor (mean |d| 3.8 deg over 4 frozen discs), not a count.

dimensions.name: rim seat radius
dimensions.metric: the radius at which the coin's flat field ends and the raised rim begins, read off a polar unwrap of every usable reference, vs EDGE.dime.field.full
dimensions.locus: _jd4band.json; radii corrected by _jd6edge.json so each photograph's own silhouette is 47.00
dimensions.method: E3, the picture: the coin redrawn in (angle, radius) with a 0.25-unit ladder over r 41.5-46.0 (_jd7seat.mjs), read at reading magnification. E1 (field departure, _jn5rim.mjs's rule generalised to |m - L|) and E2 (gradient shoulder) are published beside it in _jd4band.json and DISAGREE by up to 3.4 units, because on the cameo proof the MIRROR FIELD throws specular highlights at r 41.5-43.5 over a third of the circle and every profile-threshold estimator locks onto them. §4.3's wrong-feature failure, caught by the overlay.
dimensions.equivalence: my E1, given _jn5rim.mjs's own parameters and discs, reproduces its nickel seats EXACTLY on nickel-rev.jpg (44.05) and nickel-rev-2.png (44.30) and to within one 0.05-unit radial step on nickel-obv.jpg (44.20 vs 44.15).
dimensions.silhouette_check: estimator B (background departure) puts each photograph's own silhouette at 46.94 / 47.08 / 46.74 / 47.01 against a definitional 47.00, spreads 0.07-1.59%. `_jp7edge.mjs`'s max-gradient rule (estimator A) returns 45.25-46.94 with 3.7-8.6% spreads because it locks onto the REEDED EDGE, not the silhouette.
